name: TUTORIAL
_note: Options are NEVER shuffled in tutorial mode, and the deck is never reshuffled. The step scripts below address answers by their position in this file, so reordering an options array silently breaks the tour. The correct answer is deliberately in a different slot in each question so nobody learns that the answer is always A.

questions.q: Police can stop you on the street and start asking you questions. Are you allowed to decide not to answer?

options.explanation: You are allowed to not answer. That is what the right to remain silent means.
Being a kid does not remove the right. It belongs to everybody.
You do not need anybody standing next to you to use it.

questions.hint: There is a right with the word silent in it.
questions.principle: You do not have to answer questions from police, and that is true for kids too. This one is easy on purpose. Right now you are learning the buttons, not the law. The rest of the game is where the real questions live.

keyPhrase.quote: I don't want to answer questions.
keyPhrase.gloss: Say it out loud. Going quiet is not the same as saying it.

scenario.setup: An officer starts asking you about something that happened down the block.

lines.label: OFFICER
lines.text: Just tell me what you saw.

lines.label: YOU
lines.text: I don't want to answer questions.

lines.label: YES
lines.text: You said it out loud, so it counts.

lines.label: NO
lines.text: You go quiet, and the questions keep coming anyway.

tour.title: THIS IS A QUESTION
tour.body: Every question is a real situation. Read it, then pick from the four answers below.

tour.title: FOUR CHOICES
tour.body: One is right. Tap the one you think it is.

tour.title: TAP THIS ONE
tour.body: Go ahead. Nothing happens until you lock it in.

tour.title: LOCK IT IN
tour.body: Picking is not the same as answering. This is the part that counts.

tour.title: RIGHT OR WRONG
tour.body: You find out straight away, and you always see the correct answer.

tour.title: KEEP GOING
tour.body: Now the part that actually teaches you something.

tour.title: THREE CARDS
tour.body: The law behind it, a phrase to remember, and how it plays out in real life. These come up after every single answer.

tour.title: I UNDERSTAND
tour.body: Tap this when you have read the card. On a right answer it is also worth a point.

tour.title: NEXT CARD
tour.body: Read all three. Then you move on.

questions.q: Police start asking you questions and you decide to just go completely silent. Does staying quiet count as using your right to remain silent?

options.explanation: Going quiet is not the same as saying you are using the right. Questions can keep coming.

options.text: No, you have to say it out loud
Only if you stay quiet long enough
options.explanation: There is no amount of time that turns silence into a request.

options.text: Only if they read you your rights first
options.explanation: The right is yours either way. Saying it out loud is what uses it.

questions.hint: Silence is not a sentence. You have to say something to use it.
questions.principle: The right to remain silent has to be claimed out loud. Saying nothing at all is not the same as saying that you do not want to answer, and questioning can carry right on. This is the single most common way people lose a right they thought they were already using.
questions.safetyNote: Say it once, calmly, and then stop talking. Arguing about it on the street is not the same as using it.

scenario.setup: The questions keep coming and you decide to say nothing at all.

lines.label: OFFICER
lines.text: You can make this easy on yourself.

lines.label: YES
lines.text: You said it, so it is on the record and it counts.

lines.label: NO
lines.text: You stare at the ground and the questions keep coming.

tour.title: THREE LIVES
tour.body: You start every round with three. Getting one wrong costs a life, but the round keeps going.

tour.title: TAP THIS ONE
tour.body: This one is wrong, and we want you to pick it. Easier to show you what happens than to explain it.

tour.title: LOCK IT IN
tour.body: Go on.

tour.title: THAT COST A LIFE
tour.body: Two left. Lose all three and the round ends, but one wrong answer never does.

tour.title: THE CARDS STILL COME
tour.body: Getting it wrong is exactly when you need the explanation, so you always get it.

tour.title: NO POINTS ON A MISS
tour.body: Same three cards, same everything. You just do not earn from them this time.

questions.q: You need a lawyer and your family has no money to pay for one. What happens?

options.explanation: Money is not what decides it. A lawyer gets appointed either way.
There is no bill waiting for you afterward.

options.text: Your parents have to find one
options.explanation: Nobody in your family has to go looking. You ask, and one is appointed.

questions.hint: The price of a lawyer is not what decides whether you get one.
questions.principle: If you cannot afford a lawyer, the court appoints one and you do not pay. That lawyer works for you and nobody else. You do not have to prove anything about money before you ask.

keyPhrase.quote: I want a lawyer, and we can't pay for one.
keyPhrase.gloss: Say both parts. The free one is yours.

scenario.setup: Somebody tells you a lawyer is expensive and you probably do not want to bother.

lines.label: YOU
lines.text: I want a lawyer, and we can't pay.

lines.label: YES
lines.text: One gets appointed, and it costs your family nothing.

lines.label: NO
lines.text: You skip asking over money that was never going to be the problem.

tour.title: YOU EARNED POINTS
tour.body: Reading those cards after a right answer earned you points. This is where you spend them.

tour.title: OPEN THE SHOP
tour.body: Tap it.

tour.title: FOUR LIFELINES
tour.body: 50/50 crosses off two wrong answers. JURY shows how other students voted. COUNSEL gives you a hint. SKIP trades the question for a different one.

tour.title: FIRST THREE ARE FREE
tour.body: One free use each of 50/50, JURY and COUNSEL. After that you buy them back with points. SKIP always costs. Tap 50/50.

tour.title: CONFIRM IT
tour.body: It always asks first, so you never spend one by accident.

tour.title: TWO ARE GONE
tour.body: Crossed off and unpickable. Two choices left, and one of them is right.

tour.title: TAP THIS ONE
tour.body: This is the right one.

questions.q: An officer asks if he can look inside your pockets. What do you say?

options.text: "Go ahead, I've got nothing to hide"
options.explanation: Saying yes gives up a right you did not have to give up, and it cannot be taken back afterward.

options.text: Say nothing and hope he stops
options.explanation: A shrug or silence can be treated as a yes. Say the words.
You can refuse on your own. Nobody has to be standing next to you.

questions.hint: A question is a question. You are allowed to answer it either way.
questions.principle: When an officer asks to search, that is a request, and you can say no. Saying no is not a crime and does not prove anything about you. They might search anyway, and if that happens you do not fight it. Say clearly that you do not agree, and let a lawyer handle it later.
questions.safetyNote: Say it once and do not block anybody. Refusing out loud is the whole job; the rest happens later with a lawyer.

keyPhrase.quote: I don't agree to a search.
keyPhrase.gloss: Say it once, calmly, and do not block anybody.

scenario.setup: You are on a bench and an officer asks to take a look.

lines.label: OFFICER
lines.text: Mind if I check your pockets?

lines.label: YOU
lines.text: I don't agree to a search.

lines.label: YES
lines.text: You said no clearly, and that stays on the record.

lines.label: NO
lines.text: A shrug counts as yes, and now nobody can argue about it later.

tour.title: STUCK? BUY A HINT
tour.body: Open the shop again and take COUNSEL.

tour.title: COUNSEL
tour.body: A lawyer points you in the right direction without giving it away. Tap it.

tour.title: THERE'S YOUR HINT
tour.body: It narrows it down. It does not answer it for you.

tour.title: YOUR TURN
tour.body: This is the one.

questions.q: You are stopped by police and it is not going well. What matters most right then?

options.explanation: Being right does not help you in the moment. It helps later, with a lawyer.
The last word costs more than it is worth, every single time.
Silence is a tool, not the goal. The goal is walking away fine.

questions.hint: You can win the argument later. There is one thing you cannot get back.
questions.principle: Rights get sorted out afterward, in an office or a courtroom, with a lawyer. The street is not where anybody decides who was right. Stay calm, keep your hands where they can be seen, and deal with the rest when you are safe. That is the first thing this game told you and it is the last thing it will tell you.
questions.safetyNote: Everything else in this game is second to this.

keyPhrase.gloss: Almost everything else can be fixed later.

scenario.setup: The stop feels wrong and you can feel yourself getting louder.

lines.label: YOU
lines.text: I'm going to deal with this later.

lines.label: YES
lines.text: You go home, and a lawyer takes it from there.

lines.label: NO
lines.text: You win the argument and lose the night.

tour.title: WHERE YOU ARE
tour.body: Green is right, red is wrong, and the bar shows the whole round at a glance.

tour.title: LAST ONE
tour.body: No help on this one. You already know the answer, because it was the first thing we told you.

tour.title: GETTING HOME SAFE
tour.body: Always this one.

tour.title: THAT'S THE WHOLE GAME
tour.body: Read the cards, then go play it for real.
